Implement sealed Agent Capability Manifests for Plugins, Skills, and MCP (#197)

codeon:
  version: 1
  authority: fewensa-62
  description: |-
    ## Objective
    
    Attach an explicit operator-owned Agent Capability Manifest to every Agent Runtime Profile, covering Plugins, standalone Skills, and third-party MCP servers. Preflight, inject, seal, and read back expected-versus-observed capability evidence without allowing ambient or repository configuration to expand execution authority. This realizes GitHub issue #118.
    
    ## Precondition
    
    Provider-scoped Agent Runtime Profiles are complete and authoritative. Do not add a second runtime-profile identity or fallback to singleton provider config.
    
    ## Capability Manifest contract
    
    Each runtime profile may define provider-specific inputs that normalize to one provider-neutral durable snapshot. Example intent:
    
    ```toml
    [execution.agent_runtime_profiles.codex.openai.capabilities]
    plugins = ["helixbox/codebase"]
    standalone_skill_roots = ["/operator/codex/skills"]
    mcp_servers = ["github"]
    
    [execution.agent_runtime_profiles.cursor.default.capabilities]
    plugin_dirs = ["/operator/cursor/plugins/codebase"]
    mcp_servers = ["github"]
    
    [execution.agent_runtime_profiles.grok.xai.capabilities]
    plugin_dirs = ["/operator/grok/plugins/codebase"]
    mcp_servers = ["github"]
    ```
    
    The operator manifest is an allowlist, not arbitrary Repository/Issue input.
    
    ## Required durable snapshot
    
    During binding preparation resolve and persist:
    
    - provider/runtime-profile identity;
    - manifest revision and canonical digest;
    - Plugin identities, versions/digests, canonical paths, required/optional mode;
    - standalone Skill roots and content/manifest digests where supported;
    - MCP server identities, transports, endpoint/command digests, authorized tool/catalog digests, required/optional mode;
    - secret environment-variable references only;
    - preflight status/evidence;
    - strongest available session/thread acceptance readback;
    - availability versus invocation evidence as distinct facts.
    
    Changes affect only new bindings. In-flight bindings must not silently gain or lose capability inventory.
    
    ## Authority and collision rules
    
    - Reserve Codeon Operation completion/progress/requirements tools and all `codeon_*` names.
    - Reject any third-party tool-name/server identity collision.
    - Repository-local `.codex`, `.cursor`, `.grok`, Plugin, Skill, or MCP files cannot expand the manifest.
    - Do not inherit arbitrary ambient MCP servers, Plugin dirs, or Skill roots from HOME.
    - A capability being installed/available is not evidence that it was invoked; record these separately.
    
    ## Required/optional behavior
    
    - Missing, disabled, malformed, unauthenticated, or identity-mismatched required capabilities fail before repository mutation.
    - Optional capability failure records durable degraded evidence but allows execution.
    - Bound startup/tool time, result bytes, concurrency, and failure isolation independently per third-party MCP server.
    - Unknown or ambiguous provider readback is explicit; never claim runtime acceptance when only preflight evidence exists.
    
    ## Provider mapping
    
    ### Codex
    
    - Run inventory/preflight under the exact runtime profile/CODEX_HOME/native profile.
    - Use supported Plugin/MCP list/readback surfaces and official Skill discovery semantics.
    - Start/reuse App Server runtimes only when the sealed capability manifest is compatible.
    - Capture thread/session evidence when available; otherwise label proof as preflight-only.
    
    ### Cursor
    
    - Pass only approved repeatable `--plugin-dir` paths.
    - Compose temporary project MCP configuration from the Codeon Operation server plus the approved third-party set.
    - Preserve/restore existing guarded project config.
    - Use ACP/CLI inventory evidence to prove accepted servers/tools where supported.
    
    ### Grok
    
    - Pass only approved Plugin dirs and selected native Agent profile.
    - Preflight exact Plugin/MCP inventory under the runtime-profile homes.
    - Combine approved third-party MCP servers with the Codeon Operation server in ACP session creation.
    - Capture accepted inventory evidence when supported.
    
    ## Security
    
    - Canonicalize and verify Plugin/Skill paths; apply non-symlink/trusted-root/writability policy.
    - Verify executable and Plugin directory identity before/after spawn where replacement races matter.
    - Explicitly define transport and identity for every MCP server.
    - Child environments are allowlisted; credentials never enter repository, PostgreSQL, prompt, logs, errors, or durable manifest.
    - Provider sandbox/approval policy remains effective for Plugin hooks and MCP tools.
    - Store safe digests/references and bounded summaries only.
    
    ## Read model output
    
    Provide a transport-neutral sanitized expected-versus-observed inventory and invocation summary for the later runtime API. It must include evidence strength, observed time/freshness, degraded/failure reason, and active binding references without secret or raw payload data.
    
    ## Non-goals
    
    - Installing/upgrading Plugins or Skills during task execution.
    - Letting Agents discover and authorize arbitrary servers.
    - Treating installation as proof of use.
    - Replacing Codeon Operation completion with third-party tools.
    - Adding public HTTP routes.
    
    ## Verification
    
    For Codex, Cursor, and Grok:
    
    - required test Skill/Plugin is visible and invoked with evidence;
    - authorized test MCP tool invocation is observed with bounded result;
    - missing required capability stops before repository mutation;
    - missing optional capability proceeds with degraded evidence;
    - `codeon_*` collision is rejected;
    - unapproved repository-local MCP/Plugin is not loaded;
    - restart/config change does not alter sealed in-flight inventory;
    - exact runtime-profile isolation holds.
    
    Also test path trust, secret redaction, timeout/size/concurrency limits, PostgreSQL snapshot/replay, daemon recovery, and sanitized read-model output.
    
    ## Definition of done
    
    Every Agent binding carries a sealed, explicit, replayable capability manifest; providers receive only authorized capabilities plus Codeon's Operation server; required/optional failure behavior is deterministic; expected/observed/invoked facts are distinct; and a safe inventory projection is ready for the public runtime API.
